newsitem.title: USA: Goldman's Cohen voices caution, Wall Street pauses.
newsitem.headline: Goldman's Cohen voices caution, Wall Street pauses.

text.p: With just two words, one of Wall Street's most prominent bulls elevated the sense of caution on the U.S. stock market.
The two words -- "trading range" -- are tossed around casually on Wall Street, used to describe sideways patterns for anything from energy prices to interest rates.

But when Abby Cohen, who serves as co-chair on the investment policy committee at Goldman Sachs and Co, used the words last Friday in reference to her near-term stock market outlook, the phrase suddenly rang quite differently.
Cohen is one of Wall Street's most influential strategists and outspoken optimists. On various occasions, market sell-offs have been linked to rumors she had turned bearish.

That clout is why investment professionals took note when Cohen, in a report faxed to clients last Friday, warned investors not to expect January's sharp equity rally to continue unabated and predicted markets would soon level off.

Noting the Dow was already near her year-end target, she wrote, "We believe that equity prices could enter a trading range. As was the case in 1996, this would be accompanied by notable volatility and rotation of portfolio holdings."
As word of her forecast spread, most recently via a prominent placement on the pages of this morning's Wall Street Journal, several market analysts predicted a jittery response.

"Reading the interview today, a little voice in the back of my head told me we'd be off today," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "For people who weren't already familiar with her note, this could certainly serve as an excuse to lock in profits."
But others downplayed the potential impact of the Journal story, noting the market showed little concern in the sessions immediately following release of Cohen's remarks.
"Investors had all of Friday, Tuesday and Wednesday to respond," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "It's been out there for a week already."
